title: pvWriteVTKHDFWriter
body:
## pvWriteVTKHDFWriter

Explicit-export writer for VTKHDF (.vtkhdf), VTK's HDF5-based single-file format, suited to large meshes and to parallel or partial reading. In ParaView 5.13.3 it accepts unstructured grids, polygonal data, partitioned dataset collections and multiblock datasets. Publication uses the exact contract: ParaView re-reads the file and structure, connectivity, values and storage types must match the input exactly. Use it for compact archives of large meshes; the VTK XML writers (for example pvWriteXMLUnstructuredGridWriter) remain the most widely supported VTK format.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Image, structured and rectilinear grids are not accepted; use the matching XML writer or convert the data first.
- Higher CompressionLevel values shrink the file but make writing and reading noticeably slower.
- An earlier catalogue run (verification/2026-09-16-catalogue-expansion.json, writerQualification) passed only on a small serial fixture with default options; no current native acceptance check is recorded, so verify the export on representative data.

Native constructor: `VTKHDFWriter`. Identity: `writers/VTKHDFWriter`. Role: `writer`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Connect upstream object to `Input` | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":true,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkUnstructuredGrid","vtkPolyData","vtkPartitionedDataSetCollection","vtkMultiBlockDataSet"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ChunkSize` | Chunk Size controls the size of HDF5 datasets chunks. Chunk size can impact multi-process reading performance and compression efficiency. | `{"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `CompressionLevel` | Compression level controls how much user wants to compress the written data. Using a higher level of compression will decrease file size but significantly slow down read and write operations. | `{"maximum":9,"minimum":0,"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `0` |

Output publication contract:

```json
{
  "comparison": "exact",
  "extensions": [
    "vtkhdf"
  ],
  "filenames": "managed output directory",
  "losses": [],
  "qualification": "requires fixture",
  "time": "one scheduled state"
}
```

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

Coverage and unbound native properties:

```json
{
  "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options",
  "gaps": {},
  "origin": "generated",
  "output": "explicit exports with semantic readback",
  "outputPorts": 0,
  "qualification": "not-run"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `scenes[].exports`; writers cannot be graph nodes. The main data input is `node`; non-data ports go in `resources`.

```json
{
  "id": "exportResult",
  "node": "DATA_NODE",
  "writer": "pvWriteVTKHDFWriter"
}
```
